name: PCA Peel

lead: PCA Peel is a line of professional chemical peels from PCA Skin, used for general skin renewal and pigment concerns. People book it for fresher, more even-looking skin.

The signature peel is described by the company as a modified Jessner's formula (lactic, salicylic, kojic and citric acids with resorcinol), with TCA and lactic acid blends in the wider range. The acids exfoliate the skin surface, and the skin sheds and renews. The company reports its own clinical testing, and no independent published trials of the PCA Peel were found.

paras: It is applied in a clinic or esthetician's treatment room, often as a series of sessions. The brand describes its peel as self-neutralizing, and users commonly combine it with home skincare and sunscreen.
Peels can cause irritation, burning, redness and peeling; consumer reviews cited in one source mention these. Pigment change is a general peel risk, and sun protection matters afterward.

angle.text: People use PCA Peels to freshen dull skin and even out pigment. Acid blends loosen the outer skin, which sheds and renews, revealing a brighter, more even surface. Claims come from the manufacturer, and no independent published trials were found.

lead: PCA Peel is a line of professional chemical peels sold by the skincare company PCA Skin and applied by estheticians and other providers to improve how skin looks: smoother texture, more even tone, less visible fine lines and clearer skin. According to a summary of the company's own materials, the brand was founded in 1990 and in 2017 Colgate-Palmolive announced it would acquire PCA Skin, a deal completed in January 2018.[1]

The flagship product is described by the company as a modified, enhanced Jessner's peel combining lactic, salicylic, kojic and citric acids with resorcinol, marketed as self-neutralizing, with TCA-and-lactic-acid blends in the wider range.[1] The company's own site describes its peels as combining exfoliants with targeted actives and says it has operated for over 35 years.[2]

Chemical peels in general cause a controlled injury that makes skin shed, which can reduce fine lines, acne scars and pigment.[3] The company's claims, such as being the leading peel brand among estheticians and more than one million peels performed yearly, come from its own materials and have not been independently verified.[1][2] No independent clinical studies of the PCA Peel were found.
infobox: Lactic, salicylic, kojic, citric acids; resorcinol; TCA blends in range

paras: The company says its peels exfoliate, stimulate collagen and address fine lines, hyperpigmentation, acne and some sensitive-skin conditions with minimal downtime.[1] It states formulas are developed in-house by a PhD chemist and tested clinically, though no specific studies are cited in the source summary.[1]

Wikipedia describes chemical peels as removing the outermost layers of skin through a controlled injury. Alpha hydroxy acids such as lactic and citric acid are the mildest and treat fine wrinkles, dryness, uneven pigmentation and acne; salicylic acid, a beta hydroxy acid, is oil-soluble and used for acne and sebum; trichloroacetic acid (TCA) peels are medium-depth peels done in offices or outpatient centres.[3] Jessner's peel is used by clinicians in some protocols to prepare the skin for deeper peels.[3]

Light peels cause mainly stinging, medium peels often a warm or burning sensation, and mild to moderate redness is expected afterwards. Deeper peels carry more complications, including photosensitivity, prolonged redness, pigment changes and texture changes.[3]

The same company-based summary notes a low aggregate consumer rating on one review site from a small number of reviews, citing irritation, burning and peeling, alongside a few reviews praising results.[1] Small review samples are not representative research.

No studies found. A search of ClinicalTrials.gov returned a 2016 registered trial of cosmeceutical therapy alongside facial rejuvenation procedures (NCT02726451, 20 participants, completed), but it is not clearly a study of the PCA Peel.[4]

timeline.event: Colgate-Palmolive completes acquisition of PCA Skin.[1]
